verses.mystical_translation: Why do the nations rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?
The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the the Living Presence, and against his anointed, saying,
Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.
He that sits in the heavens shall laugh: the the Living Presence shall have them in derision.
Contemplatively, this verse gives voice to the longing that violence, deceit, domination, and fear lose their power; it is not a directive against human enemies.
Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion, the holy center.
I will declare the decree: the the Living Presence has said to me, You are my Son; this day have I begotten you.
Ask of me, and I shall give you the nations for your inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession.
You shall break them with a rod of iron; you shall dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.
Be wise now therefore, O you kings: be instructed, you judges of the earth.
Serve the the Living Presence with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Contemplatively, this verse gives voice to the longing that violence, deceit, domination, and fear lose their power; it is not a directive against human enemies.

contemplative_note: Power is accountable to a horizon larger than itself; refuge matters more than domination.
safety_note: Ancient royal and conquest poetry is not authorization for theocracy, imperialism, nationalism, collective punishment, or violence against modern nations.
